claims.content: The C2 JU transfers reporting responsibility for a track to another unit when specific conditions are met, such as receiving a Drop Track message or loss of remote reports, ensuring continuous and accurate surveillance data exchange.

goal.raw_text: The C2 JU transfers reporting responsibility for a track to another unit when specific conditions are met, such as receiving a Drop Track message or loss of remote reports, ensuring continuous and accurate surveillance data exchange.

claims.content: C2 JU

The unit originating a J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report always retains reporting responsibility, and it is illegal to assume reporting responsibility for another unit's report unless specific exceptions apply (e.g., received in a J14.0 message).
A C2 JU shall assume reporting responsibility (R2) of an Interface Unit (IU) if a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds.
A C2 JU shall assume reporting responsibility (R2) of an Interface Unit (IU) if a J2 PPLI message (other than J2.0) is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence.
A C2 JU shall assume reporting responsibility (R2) of an Interface Unit (IU) if a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU.
A C2 JU shall assume reporting responsibility (R2) of an Interface Unit (IU) if the Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0.

A JU receiving a J7.0 message with the Track Management Action field set to value 0 (Drop Track Report) on a locally held track shall assume R2 at the next opportunity if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.
Common tracking involves sharing a common track number and shifting reporting responsibility (R2) between C2 JUs to prevent cluttering the tactical plot.

The C2 JU initiates transfer of reporting responsibility when it receives a J7.0 Drop Track message, fails to receive a J2 PPLI message for 40–60 seconds, receives a J2 PPLI with NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, or detects Geodetic Position Quality set to 0 in a J2 PPLI message.

trigger.raw_text: The C2 JU initiates transfer of reporting responsibility when it receives a J7.0 Drop Track message, fails to receive a J2 PPLI message for 40–60 seconds, receives a J2 PPLI with NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, or detects Geodetic Position Quality set to 0 in a J2 PPLI message.

claims.content: The C2 JU assumes reporting responsibility (R²) if it has not received a remote report on a locally held Air or Surface track for approximately 40 seconds, or on a Land track for approximately 120 seconds.

Upon receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on a locally held track, the JU shall assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track, provided local reporting eligibility remains and no remote report has been received.

A C2 JU assumes R² of an Interface Unit if a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, or if a J2 PPLI is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, or if the Geodetic Position Quality is set to 0.
The JU retains reporting responsibility until it is relinquished in accordance with specific rules or until the track is dropped.
The JU relinquishes R² for a real-time track upon reception of a remote track report where the remote Track Quality (TQ) is greater than the local TQ.
If the remote TQ is equal to the local TQ, the JU relinquishes R² if the remote report comes from a JU whose Source Track Number (STN) is greater than the local STN.
A C² JU shall assume R² of an IU if a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds.
A C² JU shall assume R² of an IU if a J2 PPLI message (other than J2.0) is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence.
A C² JU shall assume R² of an IU if a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU.
A C² JU shall assume R² of an IU if the Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0.
A JU assumes R² if it has not received a remote report on a locally held Air or Surface track for approximately 40 seconds, or on a Land track for approximately 120 seconds.

A JU receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a locally held track shall assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and no remote report has been received.
A JU without R² for a nonreal-time track with TQ=0 shall assume R² when the track is locally updated by a new nonreal-time report.

A JU receiving a J2 PPLI message with NPS Indicator set to Inactive, Conditional Radio Silence, or TDS Failure from a JU that has R² of a locally held track may assume R² at the next opportunity if local reporting eligibility remains and no remote report has been received.

If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received on a reference point, line, area, or ground point, the current reporting responsibility (R²) unit is declared inactive, and another JU may assume R² by operator action only using the same Reference TN(s).
If no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals on a reference point, line, area, or ground point, another JU may assume R² by operator action only.

For emergency points, if a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received, the unit with R² is declared inactive, or if no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may assume R² by operator action only.
A C² JU shall assume R² of an Interface Unit if a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, which serves as an exception trigger when normal reporting fails.

A C² JU shall assume R² of an Interface Unit if a J2 PPLI message (other than J2.0) is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, indicating an exception condition requiring takeover.
A C² JU shall assume R² of an Interface Unit if a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU, triggering an exception path for responsibility transfer.
A C² JU shall assume R² of an Interface Unit if the Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0, indicating invalid position data and triggering an exception handling path.

After assuming reporting responsibility (R²) of an Interface Unit (IU), the C² JU reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG with Identity reported as Friend, and maintains the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator as value 1 if another C² JU assumes R² of the IU.

For subsurface tracks, if a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received or a J3.4 message is not received for two consecutive periodic updates, another JU may assume reporting responsibility using a different Track Number.

For emergency points, after transfer, the latest JU to report the point has reporting responsibility (R²) for that point and shall use the same TN Reference and TN Previously Reported as the previous reporting unit.

For J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB reports, the originating unit always retains reporting responsibility; it is illegal for another unit to assume reporting responsibility unless the report is received in a J14.0 message.

For ballistic missile tracks, a JU with R² relinquishes it upon receiving a remote real-time track report, and a JU assumes R² if its local TQ exceeds the received TQ by 1 or more, or if no remote report is received for 25 seconds on a locally held track.
